website.note: Skipped - 10-K + ctgov sufficient; single product candidate Acclaim CI well-characterized

ctgov.note: Trials are Class III medical device studies (no drug Phase classification); pivotal IDE study NCT06699797 confirmed via ctgov API search by intervention.

pipeline.modality: Class III implantable medical device (fully implanted cochlear implant; piezoelectric middle-ear sensor + implanted sound processor + rechargeable implanted battery)
pipeline.target: Severe-to-profound sensorineural hearing loss (auditory nerve stimulation via cochlear electrode array)
pipeline.license_origin: Internal (Envoy Medical, building on prior Esteem FI-AMEI implantable sensor technology)

indications.highest_phase: Pivotal IDE study (device equivalent of P3); FDA Breakthrough Device Designation 2019
indications.trial_name: Pivotal Clinical Trial Evaluating the Safety and Efficacy of the Fully Implanted Acclaim Cochlear Implant
indications.trial_design: Prospective, multicenter, non-randomized, open-label IDE pivotal study; 56 patients enrolled and followed 12 months; primary efficacy endpoint = CNC word speech-perception change from baseline to 12 months; staged design (FDA approval to advance to Stage 2 received Oct 3 2025); enrollment of all 56 patients completed Mar 10 2025; total study duration ~2.5 years
indications.trial_status: Active, not recruiting (enrollment complete; in 12-month follow-up)
key_milestones: 2010: predecessor Esteem FI-AMEI received FDA approval (~1,000 devices implanted)
2019: Acclaim CI received FDA Breakthrough Device Designation
2022: FDA-approved IDE for Early Feasibility Study at Mayo Clinic (3 patients implanted Q4)
Mar 10 2025: pivotal study enrollment of 56 patients completed
Oct 3 2025: FDA approval to advance from Stage 1 to Stage 2 of pivotal study
Next: 12-month follow-up readout, then PMA submission to FDA (review 6-12 months); CE Mark planned shortly after FDA approval

marketed_devices.name: Esteem FI-AMEI
indications_marketed: Sensorineural hearing loss (fully implanted active middle ear implant)
marketed_devices.note: Predecessor product; Envoy seeks reclassification as Fully Implanted Active Middle Ear Implant

excluded_legacy_terminated.reason: EFS at Mayo Clinic (3 subjects, Q4 2022) completed; superseded by ongoing pivotal study NCT06699797

summary_counts.note: Pivotal IDE study reported as P3-equivalent for medical device
